doc.title: Joel Dorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2007

title: The Ray Charles movie and Fathead's portrayal
summary: Dorn liked the Ray Charles film but objects to how it portrayed Fathead Newman, whom he saw recently at Dizzy's.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: What did you think of the Ray Charles movie?

I liked it. I thought it was terrific. I didn’t dig the way they made Fathead look, ‘cause that is nothing like he is. You know, even in his worst drug days when he was a young man he was a gentleman. They used him as like an evil foil. He didn’t turn Ray Charles — I mean I liked the movie, I thought Jamie Foxx was great you know. I liked it. I like what Taylor did, the whole thing. But I don’t like the way they made Fathead look and neither does Fathead. I will see Taylor Hackford some day and we’ll discuss this.
It was wrong man. Really wrong. What a terrible thing to do to somebody.

I saw him last week at Dizzy’s with Lonnie Smith. It’s Fathead. It’s not like we’re talking about some guy that plays weddings in Wyoming, it’s Fathead. Beautiful, and a beautiful cat. Did not deserve that portrayal. But I thought the movie by and large was pretty good.
